payload.name: Resolve Relative Event Start Dates
payload.description: During extraction, when a message describes an event or state start with a relative time phrase (e.g., 'a few days ago', 'last week', 'recently'), apply this guidance to set the correct world_start.
content: When a message describes an event or state start with a relative time phrase (e.g., 'a few days ago', 'last month', 'recently'), resolve the start date from the message/session timestamp by subtracting the indicated duration; never use the message date as the event start unless the phrase explicitly says 'today' or 'now'.
For vague phrases like 'a few days ago', record an approximate earlier date in world_start and preserve the original relative wording in memory content so the uncertainty remains traceable.
Keep this resolution consistent across extraction and any later ADD/UPDATE/MERGE; do not drop the relative expression in favor of an overly precise date.

solves: When extracting the start date of an event or state from a message that uses a relative time expression (e.g., 'a few days ago', 'last week'), the agent incorrectly sets the event's world_start to the message timestamp, losing the temporal offset. This skill teaches the agent to resolve the relative expression against the message/session timestamp and preserve the nuance.
